summary: No province-specific anti-trans law or official hostility was found; criminal law and human-rights protection are federal and uniform, and Ontario's government has not legislated on trans names, pronouns or care as two other provinces have. Police-reported hate crime across all motivations is the highest among the provinces (16.0 per 100,000 in 2024) - an all-motivations statistic, not trans-specific. Toronto and Ottawa anchor large, organised 2SLGBTQ+ communities with institutional support. Risk broadly at parity with the national picture.

sources.summary: Statistics Canada's release "Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024" (30 Mar 2026): 4,882 hate crimes reported nationally, +1% over 2023 (rate 11.9 per 100,000, -2%); incidents targeting gender identity or expression rose for a fourth consecutive year, +8% to 139 (nearly tripled, +184%, since 2020), and of known specific motivations more than half (56 of 98) targeted intersex, transgender, agender or non-binary people; sexual-orientation-motivated crimes fell 26% to 658 but remain above pre-2023 levels, with June (Pride season) running about twice the monthly average. National series - the release shows no trans-specific provincial pattern for this division.
